title: Open WebUI chat completions -- T1565.001 channel-prefixed chat_id overwrites a message in a channel the caller cannot access
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59714 (GHSA-x2ff-v5v8-m75m,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH -- corrected 2026-09-04 via live GHSA lookup, the rule's
original authoring understated this score), affecting Open WebUI chat
completions from v0.9.5 until v0.10.0.

Submitting a chat completion request with a `channel:`-prefixed
`chat_id` skipped the entire ownership/membership verification block
in `main.py` -- the code path was written to treat channel chats as
not requiring the check, with no channel membership/write check
substituted in its place. The caller-supplied `message_id` (or, for
multimodel requests, each value of the `message_ids` map) then flows
unchecked into `_make_channel_emitter()` in `socket/main.py`, which
performs a direct primary-key `Messages.update_message_by_id()` write
with no `channel_id`/`user_id` validation. Any authenticated user can
therefore overwrite a message in a private or DM channel they do not
belong to, with the model's (or a provider-error) content replacing
it while the original author attribution is preserved --
impersonation via message-integrity destruction. A v0.9.6 partial fix
validated only the first entry of the multimodel `message_ids` map,
leaving the fan-out variant exploitable until v0.10.0.

Detection logic flags a chat-completions request whose `chat_id`
carries the `channel:` prefix together with a caller-supplied
`message_id` (or `message_ids` map) -- the exact unauthenticated
write path this advisory describes, on the endpoint whose sibling
REST channel routes correctly return 403 for the same caller.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, consolidating two independent reports and citing the
exact functions and source files for both the single-model and
multimodel variants), fixed in v0.10.0.
